title: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, Xi'an
summary: The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi'an, China, was initiated in 652 by the monk Xuanzang to keep Buddhist statues and scriptures he brought back from India. It is a square brick tower of seven storeys, more than 64 metres tall, renovated several times; one source says its present form dates from the Ming dynasty.

uncertainty.note: 652 is the year the pagoda was initiated (China Daily; China Highlights says erected 652). Rebuilt in 704 and renovated in the Ming dynasty (China Highlights, China Daily). End is the present.
